content:
marina: Heads-up, bringing up zenith-v1 (q5) on staging showed a weird failure case with Cantonese vertical text that contains embedded Arabic phrases. Repro below, small thread to triage. @kenji @li-wei :eyes:

kenji: ugh, mixed-orientation + bidi + quantization = classic. can you paste the minimal input + outputs?

marina: here — input is a short vertical subtitle snippet we found in the corpora: 
```
張小姐：‎السلام عليكم
(下一行) 12:30
```
expected (fp16): 
```
張小姐：السلام عليكم
(下一行) 12:30
```
observed (zenith-v1 q5): 
```
張小姐：السلام عليكم
(下一行) 30:21  <-- time reversed
```
Weird numeric flip only happens when the Arabic phrase is present and when orientation is vertical. No flip on horizontal layout.

li-wei: can you dump tokenizer outputs for the three cases (fp16, q5, and our tokenizer-only)? could be token boundary shift causing re-rank differences.

marina: yup, tokenizer dumps attached inline: (showing token ids, spaces added)
```
# fp16 tokens: [421, 1023, 88, 9901, 765, 12, 45]
# q5 tokens:  [421, 1023, 88, 9901, 765, 12, 45]
# tokens after detokenizer (fp16): "張小姐： Salaam عليكم 
 (下一行) 12:30"
# tokens after detokenizer (q5 runtime beam 5 final): "張小姐： Salaam عليكم 
 (下一行) 30:21"
```
So token ids match but final surface string differs after the re-ranking/beam selection.

olga: that suggests beam ordering or scoring parity broke post-quant. can you run single-beam greedy and compare? if greedy matches fp16, it's a beam-rescoring/regression.

marina: greedy (beam=1) on q5 -> matches fp16 (12:30). beam=5 -> flips. So it's beam-related.

sam: could be a float tie/score inversion when logprobs quantized produce same score bucket and our lexicographic tie-breaker ends up preferring reversed tokens. we had a change in beam tie policy for speedups. @eval-bot can you show the diff of beam scores for the top two hypotheses?\
eval-bot: beam scores (logprob) snapshot:
```
# fp16 beam top2:
H1 score: -12.345678
H2 score: -12.356000
# q5 beam top2:
H1 score: -12.350000
H2 score: -12.349999  <-- tiny inversion
```
Note: quantization caused scores to be binned, small differences lead to tie-breaker taking H2 on q5.

li-wei: what's in H1 / H2? show token sequences for H1/H2 around the numeric span.

marina: H1 (expected ordering): ... ["12", ":", "30"]
H2 (wrong): ... ["30", ":", "21"]
Both hypotheses identical earlier, only later tokens diverge slightly.

olga: do we apply length penalty or numeric normalization in postprocess for vertical mode? Could be postprocess bug triggered only when bidi markers present.

marina: postprocess is the same, but we do call locale_norm for vertical layouts to preserve punctuation anchors. Still, the flip persists even if we disable locale_norm.

kenji: action plan: 1) add deterministic tie-breaker that preserves lexical order for numeric sequences (hotfix) 2) add small score jitter based on fp16 reference when quantized score bins are equal (temporary) 3) reproduce on Dedicated machines (to rule out kernel nondeterminism). I'll take 1 and 3.

sam: also file a regression test in the eval harness: create a tiny test that injects mixed Cantonese vertical + Arabic + timestamp and asserts exact token order across quant variants. tag as blocking for q5 rollout.

marina: already added a smoke test in my branch and a failing sample to the qual notebook. PR: https://git.redwood/zenith/onboard/PR-432 (internal).

eval-bot: quick metrics: on the library eval set (N=12k multilingual subtitles) q5 currently shows -0.6 BLEU delta on vertical-language subset vs fp16, mostly concentrated on small numeric spans and bracketed timestamps.

li-wei: can you dump the random seed / nondet flags used on q5 run? we should confirm it's deterministic with beam_size and no sampling.

marina: run flags: --seed 42 --deterministic True --beam_size 5 --length_penalty 0.6 --locale vertical_cjk.

olga: good. Next steps: kenji re-run on dedicated + kernel-assert logs, sam add test, li-wei bisect whether tie-breaker change introduced in runtime PR #1204 or quant kernel rounding introduced in q5 pack. I'll own bisect.

kenji: assigning myself dedicated rerun now. will report within the hour. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

marina: thanks all. If anyone hits similar mixed-orientation numeric flips, ping this thread. I'll keep the failing sample pinned in the qual repo. :pushpin:

sam: fyi, leaving a note for product that this is a rare regression affecting vertical subtitle workflows for APAC partners — no large-scale impact detected yet but sensitive for user-facing captions.

eval-bot: note added to incident tracker: INC-2027 (suspect: quant score binning + beam tie-breaker).

kenji: rerun complete on Dedicated (gpu-node-gamma). reproduces. kernel logs show same score inversion. next: try float-emulation mode for q5 (slow) to confirm rounding effect.

marina: cool, will wait for the float-emulation results. thanks! :thumbsup:
